💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:17 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • It was gone 11pm when Thomas Tuchel was shaking the hands of Harry Kane’s parents on the Wembley pitch while the children of England’s record appearance maker enjoyed the run of the national stadium in front of 90,000 empty seats.
  • This was time for Kane to fully take in the emotion of an historic night alongside his family and that Tuchel was out there too felt instructive of their relationship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:17 EST, 13 November 2026.

It was gone 11pm when Thomas Tuchel was shaking the hands of Harry Kane’s parents on the Wembley pitch while the children of England’s record appearance maker enjoyed the run of the national stadium in front of 90,000 empty seats.

This was time for Kane to fully take in the emotion of an historic night alongside his family and that Tuchel was out there too felt instructive of their relationship.

Kane and Tuchel had frank conversations last month about the World Cup fallout, on how England might be best tinkering with their selection when chasing games.

The manager respects and values his captain’s opinion on these things, recognising that he is almost completely agenda-free, as they attempt to better plot a route to silverware in readiness for the European Championship in 18 months’ time.

If there was uncertainty about identity and style when the World Cup crunch arrived, when Enzo Fernandez was pulling stupid faces and the colour drained from England faces, then players have felt that the detail on how Tuchel wants to move forward has been clear across the first two camps since America.

According to recent reports, thursday night was not vintage against a Croatia team they battered 7-0 a few weeks back. Tuchel and Kane both admitted that afterwards but it is noticeable that there is a defined proposal on how they intend to attack in a slightly different way.

Thomas Tuchel embraces Harry Kane's wife Katie at Wembley on Thursday night.

Harry Kane (centre) and Co are changing the way they attack after the World Cup.

In a recent development, were Tuchel to have been able to pick a first-choice back four then the win would likely have been more comfortable, Croatia benefiting from individual errors. And a lack of cutting edge inside the box hindered the hosts too.

The idea behind what they were doing appeared well thought out though and that should bring about some gentle encouragement.

The full backs, Trent Alexander-Arnold and Lewis Hall, were both consistently worked into hugely dangerous areas in the inside channels, while the make-up of Tuchel’s midfield felt very deliberate as well.

It has been revealed that it is no coincidence that England enjoyed the highest amount of possession in the half spaces ten yards inside Croatia’s half. That is a clear directive, with both Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice drifting wider to create overloads and the full backs pushed into threatening spaces.

According to recent reports, ‘Declan understands the game like he’s almost a coach on the field and in a perfect position to manage all these things from behind,’ Tuchel noted this week. To have a constant interchanging unit, he does need brains.

These are the rotations that the Three Lions didn’t engineer enough of over in the United States, with Kane dropping deep as he does and completing that wonder crossfield pass for the Morgan Rogers opener.

They are the moments that Tuchel is preaching, Jude Bellingham taking up an unusual position in order to stretch Croatia as he squared for the Chelsea forward.

What Tuchel needs now is to work on how that can be translated into making sure his very best players can affect matches more regularly inside the opponent’s box.

Jude Bellingham only touched the ball four times in Croatia's box in the 2-1 win.

England manager Thomas Tuchel will speak to his players about what to do if racial abuse mars Sunday’s Nations League group decider against Spain in Madrid.

The England team have been on the wrong end of racism in Madrid before – back in 2004 – and refused to play a friendly there in 2008, insisting the fixture be moved to Seville.

In March this year, meanwhile, Spanish fans chanted anti-Muslim songs during a game with Egypt in Barcelona and the World champions have been subsequently ordered by FIFA to play their next friendly in a partially-closed stadium.

There will be a full house at Athletico Madrid’s Riyadh Air Metropolitano stadium as England try to topple Spain from the top of their group on Sunday and Tuchel said: ‘I think I hear about it [the Barcelona incident] for the first time that this happens. I think it's unacceptable.

‘In any stadium we will never accept racism.

Industry observers note that ‘I expect full support from the Spanish crowd for the Spanish team. But we will not expect anything else. And I think the referee in the games and the officials know about that.

‘I think we had a same discussion before the Serbia game [last year]. There is a protocol in place.

‘Yeah, maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Spain].’.

Tuchel and the FA expect a hostile atmosphere in Madrid, especially as two Real players – Jude Bellingham and Trent Alexander-Arnold - will be in the England squad.

Last year’s Serbia game passed without incident in Belgrade and the FA are confident the same will apply this weekend.

Seven years ago in Sofia, though, captain Harry Kane almost led the England team off the field after following FIFA protocols by alerting the referee to abuse aimed at Tyrone Mings, Raheem Sterling and Marcus Rashford. The game was paused while the culprits were thrown out.

‘I still think the protocol is in place and it's notable that the players know about is,’ added Tuchel.

According to recent reports, ‘And then yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. The best answers are on the pitch.’.

The FIFA protocol – adopted by UEFA and the Premier League – is a four step-process that starts with a player alerting match officials and is followed by a warning to the crowd, a possible suspension of play and, if necessary, the abandonment of the game.

That Kane only touched it six times inside the 18-yard area and Bellingham on just four occasions points to a team still figuring themselves out.

That will be put to the severe test in Madrid on Sunday. England do not beat the truly elite nations; never have.

And it’ll be interesting to see whether Tuchel sticks to this sort of strategy, one designed to dominate, or if he instead relies on the counter-attacking ability of a group he has viewed as a ‘Premier League team’ before now, leaning into their physicality.

If England are feeling confident enough, giving this tweaked style a go against the world champions might offer them some answers on what could be achieved when the proper silverware is on the line.

Quello del futuro della porta dell'Inter resta un argomento caldo in casa nerazzurra. Perché Josep Martinez non ha ancora dato le giuste garanzie e perché in giro non mancano certo le occasioni. Come quella, riferita da Tuttosport, di Alisson, che a giugno si libererà gratis dal Liverpool:.

Sources indicate that "Fra questi, c'è sicuramente Alisson Becker, ex Roma e da nove stagioni titolare del Liverpool. Il brasiliano ha l'accordo in scadenza fra sette mesi e potrebbe aver finito il suo ciclo con i Reds. Già la scorsa primavera Alisson era finito nei ragionamenti di alcuni club come Inter e poi Juventus. Per altro i nerazzurri avevano sfiorato il brasiliano già nel lontano 2009, quando a 17 anni si era messo in luce nelle giovanili della Selecao e dell'Internacional di Porto Alegre. Non se ne fece nulla e Alisson arrivò 23enne alla Roma".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lotito e Fabiani conoscono dal 15 novembre la cifra da coprire; resta il nodo della liquidità per gli acquisti.

La Lazio può ancora evitare il blocco totale del mercato invernale. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Lotito e Fabiani conoscono dal 15 novembre la cifra da coprire, ma non hanno ancora consegnato i documenti alla Commissione di controllo. Il termine è il 30 novembre; l’organismo li esaminerà a dicembre. Anche un eventuale via libera, però, non garantirebbe alla società la liquidità necessaria per acquistare senza vendere giocatori importanti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Gli acquisti estivi e l’aumento degli ingaggi hanno peggiorato l’indice del Costo del lavoro allargato, portandolo oltre il limite previsto per operare a saldo zero. Lotito lavora da mesi per rientrare attraverso crediti futuri e altri asset. Potrebbe inoltre intervenire successivamente con un’immissione di denaro, così da scongiurare il blocco e mantenere la libertà di operare sul mercato.

Recent findings suggest that after that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. Nel mercato di gennaio, Gattuso vuole preservare il gruppo che ha portato la Lazio in testa alla classifica. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Il tecnico ha ricevuto garanzie: nessuno partirà. Per definire le strategie servirà però un nuovo confronto con la società, perché le intenzioni dovranno misurarsi con i bilanci.

Industry observers note that la garanzia sulle partenze tutela il gruppo attuale. Resta da stabilire, nel confronto con il club, quali scelte di mercato siano compatibili con i bilanci.

Gattuso aveva mostrato la propria linea già a settembre, quando aveva detto no a Icardi, allora svincolato. Nella ricostruzione del quotidiano, il tecnico preferisce calciatori disposti a seguire il gruppo senza chiedere privilegi, gradi o riconoscimenti.

Industry observers note that la Lazio capolista è nata da questa impostazione. Il pallone circola tra i giocatori e la costruzione delle reti coinvolge la squadra: un modo di giocare che Gattuso vuole conservare fino alla fine.

Published: 17:03 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 13 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino already has a fresh injury headache at Manchester United - and he's not even through the door yet.

Patrick Dorgu has been sent home from Denmark duty having failed a series of physical tests.

The full-back missed four Premier League matches in October due to a hamstring injury but came on to provide an assist and score the equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Now he re-joins an injury list which includes Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Carlos Baleba, and potentially Harry Maguire, with Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko ruled out longer-term.

Denmark's team doctor Martin Boesen mentioned: 'We have carried out a series of tests on Dorgu, and he has not performed well enough to be ready to play in the two matches.

'He needs further recovery time after his injury, so we are sending him home for additional rehabilitation.'.

Patrick Dorgu has been sent home fromDenmark duty after failing a series of fitness tests.

It is potentially another thing for incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino to worry about.

Dorgu, 22, will miss matches against Portugal and Norway in the Nations League.

Pochettino will hope Dorgu makes a quick recovery as he seeks to get Manchester United back on track.

United, who sit 18th in the Premier League, agreed to pay more than £10million to prise Pochettino and his staff away from the United States national team.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick and will get down to business after his final matches in charge of the USA against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

The former Southampton, Tottenham, and Chelsea boss broke down in tears as he began his farewell and admitted that he couldn’t turn down the ‘dream’ job of Manchester United head coach.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

In a recent development, ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

The 54-year-old Argentine revealed that United first made contact on Sunday after the 4-4 draw in Carrick’s final game left the club in the relegation zone.

‘I never stated I wanted to go back in the Premier League,’ said Pochettino, whose first game in charge of United will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

‘All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear. There was some contact. When things became bigger, they are very sensitive.

It has been revealed that ‘We were very transparent with the federation and they understand the situation. The decision between US Soccer and Man United to agree to continue for these two games will not change our commitment.

‘That decision was between the three parties but, of course if Man United agreed different terms, I need to respect that.’.

  • It has been revealed that I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

In a recent development, “Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio. “So di aver lasciato qualcosa e quel cerchio lo dobbiamo chiudere. In passato ci sono stati momenti in cui avremmo potuto ritrovarci, ma è molto difficile, perché devono verificarsi due condizioni: io devo essere libero e la Juventus deve essere alla ricerca di un allenatore. Ci sono state due occasioni concrete. La prima quando la Juventus scelse Maurizio Sarri: io ero senza squadra e, alla fine, andai all’Inter. La seconda quando arrivò Giuntoli, che decise di puntare su Thiago Motta: in quel caso io finii al Napoli. Dopo Bari potevo diventare l’allenatore della Juventus, avevo parlato più volte con Castagnini e con Secco, c’era Ranieri in panchina, poi presero Ferrara per fare le ultime partite per andare in Champions. Loro sapevano benissimo che avrei fatto il 4-2-4, avendo attaccanti come Amauri, Iaquinta, Treseguet e Del Piero, dissi “con gli attaccanti siamo a posto, dobbiamo prendere degli esterni”. Loro, non so per quale motivo, presero Diego dal Werder Brema e mi chiamarono per avere delle rassicurazioni. Io vado, entro da allenatore della Juve e mi chiedono come volessi giocare e io dico “ancora? con il 4-2-4”. Mi chiesero dovre avrei messo Diego e io dissi “lo avete comprato, anche se abbiamo 4 attaccanti, lo metto al fianco alla punta”. Mi sento dire “Diego vuole giocare con il 4-3-1-2” e in quel momento pensa alla mia follia che fa capire che sono una persona dritta che non scende a compromessi. Un altro avrebbe detto “te lo faccio giocare anche in porta, basta che mi fai questo contratto”. Io forte delle mie idee e delle mie convinzioni, perchè non voglio scendere a compromessi, gli dico “se il giocatore deve decidere come giocare, non sono io l’allenatore giusto per voi”. Vado via da li ed esco che non sono più l’allenatore della Juventus”.

It has been revealed that I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut. #15316. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under substantial pressure

Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under substantial pressure

📅 13 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 31 min read (6180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~31 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • In a recent development, but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

In a recent development, but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent major players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

It has been revealed that they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

According to recent reports, the question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Sources indicate that afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical blueprint to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their upcoming head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Industry observers note that maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Recent findings suggest that was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

Sources indicate that and the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Sources indicate that patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

Industry observers note that the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but substantial moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

In a recent development, [On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

It has been revealed that changed the strategy for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

It has been revealed that we always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

We have to go home with this injustice.

According to recent reports, haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that reveals personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”.

Sources indicate that “We had to change the proposal a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

Recent findings suggest that and on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

Sources indicate that there will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

It has been revealed that but if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the major goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Recent findings suggest that martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

It has been revealed that haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

It has been revealed that united have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

In a recent development, good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a major cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Industry observers note that nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Industry observers note that fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

It has been revealed that what a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

According to recent reports, haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

In a recent development, city with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Recent findings suggest that much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3.

It has been revealed that haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

According to recent reports, strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

In a recent development, keane remarked: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”.

According to recent reports, micah Richards mentioned: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”.

🗣️ "Bruno [Fernandes] is the one who is violent here, I have to call it out"Roy Keane doesn't believe Phil Foden deserved to be sent off against Man Utd 🟥 pic.twitter.com/up5ZQqFShy.

Recent findings suggest that this fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

According to recent reports, rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

Recent findings suggest that city threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

Industry observers note that he was not a starter in Carrick’s original game initiative, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

Looks to be a secondary movement. Confirming the red card for….

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. Fernandes and Foden were scrapping for the ball near the touchline, the United man had a nibble at Foden as he tried to protect the ball. But then Foden kicked up from the ground with his studs into the midriff of Fernandes. I don’t think he can have any complaints.

Recent findings suggest that although Foden’s sending off will certainly not have enhanced his prospects! Kicking out in retaliation at being kicked by Bruno Fernandes when he was on the ground.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

The Old Trafford crowd are encouraged by what they are watching, but Enzo Fernandez takes some of the venom from their attacking momentum by winning a foul.

Recent findings suggest that then Ruben Dias clips a long ball forward over Dalot’s head which the right-back makes a mess of to Semenyo’s benefit, but the winger finds the gloves of Lammens with the cross. Just had to clear the goalkeeper and Haaland would have had an open goal.

Recent findings suggest that england manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a big game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Just before that, City invited the pressure with a stray cross-field pass in their own defensive third which Guehi could not control. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Industry observers note that rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

In a recent development, an early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

It has been revealed that maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

"THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE" banner above the tunnel#MUFC pic.twitter.com/hrs71K7r1y.

Probably keeping the emotions away, which is not easy. It’s just try to embrace the chaos, that’s it..

According to recent reports, I say chaos, [but] it can be noise. Embrace it, it’s a derby, it’s nice... Try to play our game!

We’ve got a lot of encouragement going into the season, of course we wanted more points at this stage. We understand how notable this game is and what it can do but it’s getting the balance, we know it’s a long season and we have to be consistent over a period of time. In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

It has been revealed that michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

If you had read Sam Wallace’s exclusive interview with United’s right-back you would know he was in line to make his 250th appearance for the club. Dalot did not want to take Carrick’s team selection for granted when talking about the milestone, but United’s manager is not replete with full-back options.

If you haven’t checked out the interview, you can have a read here.

Fans have chanted: “You treat us like s--- Ratcliffe and the Glazers, you treat us like s---.”.

Some supporters also targeted ambitions to build a latest 100,000 capacity stadium adjacent to Old Trafford by singing: “You can shove your new ground up your a---.”.

Inside Old Trafford, all flags in the Stretford End are set to be removed with and replaced by one banner that reads: “THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE.”.

Industry observers note that struck by the nature of both midfields. If you look over the careers of Anderson-Fernandez-Cherki and Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes, Anderson is the only player of the six who has not played as a No 10 or advanced midfielder. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

Sources indicate that “You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Recent findings suggest that enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

It has been revealed that representing the Reds on derby day... 📋❤️‍🔥COME ON UNITED! 🗣️🗣️🗣️.

According to recent reports, they are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

In a recent development, there will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

"You can shove your new ground up your a*rse"#MUFC protests pic.twitter.com/EMmnF8FhNo.

Kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

Recent findings suggest that both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Industry observers note that sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

According to recent reports, it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Per la trasferta del 28 novembre sono esauriti i 1.489 posti iniziali nel settore ospiti; restano altri tagliandi.

Per Lazio-Lecce sono attese 13.300 presenze all’Olimpico, il secondo dato stagionale più alto per una gara casalinga biancoceleste. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Corriere dello Sport, La vendita dei biglietti avanza lentamente, mentre il tifo organizzato conferma la protesta contro Lotito e la decisione di disertare le partite in casa.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Finora sono stati staccati circa 5.300 biglietti. A questi si aggiungono i 4.500 abbonati stagionali — una cifra non ufficializzata — e i 3.500 sostenitori che hanno aderito al Pack 3. Il totale provvisorio arriva così a 13.300 presenze, secondo quanto riportato dal Corriere dello Sport.

Il dato supera le 12.283 presenze registrate nell’ultima gara casalinga contro il Cagliari. Resta alle spalle soltanto delle 21.373 presenze contro il Milan, quando sugli spalti c’erano però circa 10.000 tifosi rossoneri.

L’affluenza resta lontana dalla normalità descritta per una squadra che guida da sola la classifica. Il tifo organizzato proseguirà infatti la contestazione a Lotito, nonostante i risultati ottenuti dalla formazione di Gattuso.

Industry observers note that il clima è diverso in vista del derby del 13 dicembre, indicato come l’unica eccezione alla protesta annunciata prima dell’inizio della stagione. Per la stracittadina sono già garantite 25.500 presenze, con la prospettiva di un Olimpico colorato di biancoceleste.

According to recent reports, la risposta alla prevendita è stata immediata nella seconda fase, riservata ai 29.918 abbonati della passata stagione. Il numero delle presenze garantite si avvicina a quella cifra; resta poi la fase aperta a tutti, che potrebbe portare il totale oltre quota 30.000.

It has been revealed that cresce anche l’attesa per la finale di Supercoppa italiana a San Siro. Il 23 novembre si aprirà la finestra di vendita riservata agli abbonati della stagione 2025-26. Al momento possono acquistare i biglietti soltanto gli abbonati al campionato in corso.

Industry observers note that inter premiata come squadra dell'anno al GLGS 2026: sul palco dell'evento ha parlato il presidente nerazzurro Beppe Marotta. Ecco le sue dichiarazioni: "Questo è un premio riconosciuto alla società intera: c'è una squadra che va in campo e un'altra dietro le quinte composta da circa 350 persone che quotidianamente lavorano per supportare chi va in campo. Cercando anche di non dare alibi: la macchina funziona se non ci diamo alibi. Quando non ci sono alibi, la squadra deve tirare fuori tutto l'orgoglio. Questo riconoscimento è distribuito a tutte le componenti della società.

Fondazione Inter? A breve la presenteremo, è una novità assoluta. Una società di calcio non è solo un fenomeno sportivo e di business: da tempo il nostro bilancio ha raggiunto i 538 milioni di ricavi, ma è anche un fenomeno sociale. E come tale deve agire nel contesto territoriale in cui siamo ma anche nel resto del mondo cercando di fare del bene e rendere felici i meno fortunati. Attenzione al terzo settore, abbiamo tre squadre special: i primi attori sono i calciatori, loro non se ne rendono conto ma con le loro gesta sono una fonte di felicità. Fare una fondazione è un passo minimo che ci sentiamo obbligati a fare e lo faremo con grande impegno".

Nell'intervista pre-partita, il tecnico del Lecce Di Francesco ha commentato la sfida contro la Lazio, soffermandosi sulla crescita del gruppo e sulla maggiore consapevolezza biancoceleste.

Sabato all'Olimpico arriva il Lecce per sfidare la Lazio, attualmente prima in classifica: alla vigilia del match, il tecnico giallorosso Eusebio Di Francesco ha sottolineato nella conferenza stampa l'entusiasmo dei biancocelesti, le loro qualità tecniche ed esaltato Gattuso, evidenziando la forza e la crescita del gruppo..

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, L'ultimo a essere rientrato è Gaspar, è tornato ieri sera e si è allenato con la squadra. Non ci sono stati problemi dovuti al rientro. Ho un paio di dubbi, dietro e in mezzo al campo. Davanti già so quali saranno gli interpreti di questa gara.

Ho sempre parlato di coraggio, voglio un atteggiamento propositivo, ho visto una squadra allenarsi davvero bene in queste due settimane. Sono fiducioso di quello che il gruppo mi può dare. La Lazio ha grande entusiasmo, sta facendo molto bene, ha mantenuto giocatori di qualità e ha acquisito maggiore consapevolezza nei propri mezzi. Gattuso sta facendo veramente bene. Dobbiamo giocarcela, scendendo in campo senza timore reverenziale.

In a recent development, tutto si lega al risultato, io mi voglio affidare alle caratteristiche dei calciatori più che ai sistemi di gioco. Se ho fatto certe scelte contro il Torino deriva dal fatto che non avevo esterni, oggi ho recuperato Monteiro. A Torino volevo dare consapevolezza e forza a una squadra che aveva preso tanti gol, stavamo soffrendo sulle palle alte e sul finale ho messo un difensore in più. Giocando a cinque dietro non abbiamo subito un tiro per 70 minuti. Volevamo prima di tutto fare una grande fase difensiva e ritrovare solidità e ci siamo riusciti. Per me abbiamo fatto una gara davvero importante.

Industry observers note that pierotti è un'assenza importante per le sue caratteristiche. Alle mie ali ho chiesto di lavorare nello stesso modo sia quando attaccano sia quando difendono. Lo fanno le grandi squadre, figuriamoci noi. Berisha sta sicuramente meglio, ha alternato allenamenti con la squadra a giorni di recupero per evitare ricadute, ma è un giocatore che deve acquisire la forma migliore, però mi è piaciuto. Dobbiamo avere la giusta cautela. Monteiro si è allenato con la squadra, è recuperato e può anche partire dall'inizio.

Abbiamo lavorato su come legare i tre di centrocampo coi quattro di difesa. Ma non dimentichiamoci anche della fase offensiva, i nostri attaccanti si devono ancora sbloccare, dobbiamo avere fiducia in loro.

Dobbiamo essere più squadra, quando si difende e si attacca. Abbiamo cambiato sistema di gioco poche volte, per necessità o per scelta. Questa squadra è stata costruita per giocare con il 4-3-3 o 4-2-3-1. Da qui a fine gennaio ci saranno tante partite, l'augurio è quello di poter scegliere i migliori giocatori di partita in partita.

It has been revealed that nei giorni scorsi si è parlato di un interesse concreto, da parte dell'Inter, per Oliver Provstgaard, difensore classe 2003 della Lazio. Intervenuto su Youtube, Alfredo Pedullà ne ha parlato così:.

"Non si può far vivere il 'mostro' in prima pagina, cioè per la vicenda di Provstgaard all'Inter, prenotato da adesso per la prossima estate come acconto di una situazione legata a Frattesi. Sono sincero, non ho riscontri di questo tipo, credo sia molto difficile pensare a Provstgaard all'Inter per 40 mln quando l'Inter i difensori cerca di prenderli prima quando valgono meno, guardate le esperienze passate e le operazioni che ha fatto l'Inter e magari dopo 4-5 anni provare a fare una plusvalenza a 3-4 volte in più del prezzo pagato.

Questa è la filosofia di qualsiasi società, Inter compresa. Un esempio: la Juve ha preso Alajbegovic ad una cifra importante perché spera di venderlo magari al doppio fra 4 anni, per poter fare una plusvalenza. Non esiste prendere un difensore a 40 mln perché c'è il coinvolgimento di Frattesi, non c'entra nulla, Frattesi è un discorso a parte, un affare per la Lazio e un affare eventualmente per l'Inter in caso di futura rivendita, è un'operazione per il momento da 15 mln. Accostare Provstgaard all'Inter oggi non ha logica".

#15308. SCOTLAND 2 NORTH MACEDONIA 1: John McGinn at the double to spare the blushes of Pocognoli's shaky Scots on skipper Robertson's big night

SCOTLAND 2 NORTH MACEDONIA 1: John McGinn at the double to spare the blushes of Pocognoli's shaky Scots on skipper Robertson's big night

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:11 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • On the night when the nation looked over its shoulder and celebrated the past, the here and now for Scotland looked distinctly uncertain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:11 EST, 13 November 2026.

On the night when the nation looked over its shoulder and celebrated the past, the here and now for Scotland looked distinctly uncertain.

Coming 40 years and a day after his friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish, pulled on a Scotland jersey for the 102nd and final time, Andy Robertson joined the great man on a mark which, for years, seemed beyond the reach of mere mortals.

By time up, history had mercifully repeated itself at Hampden. Back in the day, Dalglish, by then player-manager at Anfield, sailed into the international sunset on the back of a routine 3-0 win over Luxembourg.

According to recent reports, facing another opponent of modest ability, Robertson’s red letter day didn’t go quite as smoothly. Yet, when the Tottenham man is old and grey and reflecting on the night he created history, the annals will at least record a slender victory.

While his side did just about enough to prevail here, this was another fraught night for Sebastien Pocognoli.

According to recent reports, you can talk about the need for patience under the fresh manager until the cows come home. But North Macedonia are 71st in FIFA’s rankings. Scotland are 43rd.

John McGinn celebrates in trademark fashion after netting Scotland's winner from the spot.

At Hampden Park, in front of an expectant crowd, Scotland should be putting them to the sword with something to spare.

It has been revealed that yet, for long enough, the Belgian’s newly introduced-look side were flat, predictable and plodding. It said much that it took the intervention of VAR for them to get the penalty which would ultimately lead to three points being accrued.

John McGinn’s second half double saved the Belgian’s blushes and truthfully there was little else to get the Tartan Army off their seats.

Too many substantial-name players scarcely merited pass marks. Too few looked comfortable in the system the manager is trying to bed in.

Sources indicate that if it was a step in the right direction, it was a small one. After five games under the affable Belgian, the progress has certainly not been startling.

While it goes without saying that beating the Swiss in St Gallen on Monday will be an inordinately tougher task, having some hope of moving up a place and securing a kinder draw for the Euros is still better than no hope.

Regardless of what pot they end up in when the draw is made in Belfast next month, a radical improvement will certainly be required across the board if they are to stand any chance of qualifying for the tournament via the front door.

As well as the achievements of Robertson and Dalglish, the career of Craig Gordon was acknowledged before the match with the 84-times capped keeper deservedly afforded a warm hand by the Tartan Army.

McGinn slots home his penalty after Ben Gannon-Doak had been brought down in the area.

Sources indicate that there were absolutely no excuses for Scotland here. North Macedonia were a tier-two team in name only. They arrived at Hampden having not won in 12 matches and not scored in eight.

Another Pocognoli game saw another back-three combination. This time Luke Graham was selected in the centre of the unit with Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney deployed either side of the Stoke man in what were their first appearances under the Belgian.

It has been revealed that robertson and Ben Gannon-Doak were tasked with providing the width in the 3-4-3. Scott McTominay slotted back into an advanced role beside John McGinn with the returning Che Adams asked to lead the line.

Sources indicate that for all there was a healthy crowd in excess of 40,000 inside Hampden, the atmosphere was subdued. In the four Nations League games to date under the latest manager, the side hadn’t exactly given the supporters much to feed off.

In a recent development, despite some big guns returning, Scotland made a laboured start to their night’s work. It stated much that Graham, on his second appearance, was busier than any defender in white.

In a recent development, the first opening came as a result of an opposition error. John McGinn found Billy Gilmour who fed the overlapping Robertson. The skipper’s cross was well out of Adams’ reach.

Sebastien Pocognoli got his first Hampden win as Scotland boss but it was a nervy night.

Recent findings suggest that although Ljupche Doriev worried Angus Gunn with a curling effort, Scotland began to exert some degree of control on the match. Lewis Ferguson kept the visitors hemmed in with a header into McTominay’s feet. The Napoli man saw his shot on the spin well saved by Stole Dimitrievski.

Pocognoli was frustrated when Slovakian referee Michal Ocenas blew for a foul on McTominay, his justifiable gripe being that playing an advantage would have seen Robertson have a crack at goal.

It has been revealed that dimitrievski had a decent night. Although Adams’ flashing header from McGinn’s corner took a deflection, a reflex save at his near post added to Scotland’s frustration.

North Macedonia were a spirited but ordinary side. They still had enough to thwart Pocognoli’s men.

It has been revealed that gannon-Doak saw plenty of the ball down the right, yet the end product often wasn’t there. The Bournemouth man did tee up Billy Gilmour for one dangerous cross. McTominay tried to replicate his iconic overhead kick against Denmark nearly a year ago. This time, his aim wasn’t true.

You could hardly blame Pocognoli’s star man for failing to find the net on that occasion.

Scott McTominay attempts an overhead spectacular a year on from THAT goal at Hampden.

That wasn’t the case a few moments later when Adams slipped him in. Dimitrievski saved McTominay’s strike with an outstretched leg when he should have been picking the ball out of his net.

Adams had just blazed a strike high over the top while one-on-one with the keeper although the offside flag saved his blushes.

According to recent reports, the visitors came closer to edging ahead when Eljif Elmas played the pass of the match over Scotland’s static defence to pick out Ezgjan Alioski. His lay-off was smashed into the side net by Enis Bardhi.

Recent findings suggest that A wholly uninspiring first-half concluded with Robertson advancing up the left and launching a cross halfway to Castlemilk. This was not going well.

Pocognoli waited on the edge of the pitch for his players returning, his enthusiastic applause clearly audible in the arena.

Sources indicate that his hopes of a breakthrough at the outset of the second period were dashed in extraordinary fashion. Adams did well to chase a ball down to the line and cut it back. McTominay and his marker couldn’t connect, leaving Gilmour the simple task of firing into an unguarded net. Leaning back, his failure to even hit the target was unfathomable.

Elmin Rastoder celebrates after silencing Hampden with a leveller for North Macedonia.

Recent findings suggest that within seconds, the sense of relief inside Hampden was palpable as the opener finally arrived. Porteous got enough distance on his clearing header for Adams to barge Visar Musliu out of the way.

McGinn was alert to the situation and burst into the box. His crisp strike finally had the beating of the goalkeeper.

It has been revealed that it should have settled Pocognoli’s side and paved the way for a comfortable result. Instead, they were pegged back within three minutes.

It was all just so simple and so avoidable. Bardhi’s whipped corner only needed McTominay to outjump his man. Flat-footed as the delivery arrived, he could only watch on in horror as Elmin Rastoder’s flashing header beat Angus Gunn.

Sources indicate that although Gilmour worked the keeper with a low strike, North Macedonia also sniffed a second goal. Time and time again, they got into pockets of space on the flanks and fired in dangerous crosses.

Sources indicate that adams made way for Oli McBurnie, the Hull man desperately hoping for his first goal on his 21st international appearance. He had a gilt-edged chance to get off the mark when rolled in by McGinn, but selflessly passed to the overlapping Gannon-Doak.

Scotland move on to their final game away in Switzerland as they look to finish on a high note.

According to recent reports, the winger appeared to take a heavy touch which allowed the keeper to rescue the situation. VAR, however, spotted that Dimitrievski had impeded him. Penalty.

McGinn did the necessary from 12 yards, smashing the ball straight down the middle for his 24th international goal.

North Macedonia, to their credit, kept going for it. They sensed a fragility in Scotland. Everyone in the ground could.

McGinn’s calm conversion proved to be just about enough to get the job done. But it’s fair to suggest that we are still awaiting lift-off in the upcoming era.

In a recent development, SCOTLAND (3-4-1-2): Gunn; Porteous, Graham, Tierney; Gannon-Doak (Hickey 76), Ferguson, Gilmour (Christie 76), Robertson; McGinn; Adams (McBurnie 67), McTominay. Booked: Ferguson. Manager: Sebastien Pocognoli.

NORTH MACEDONIA (4-2-3-1): Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Mladenovski, Musliu, Alioski; Gashtarov (Elezi 64), Elmas (Stankovski 78); Churlinov (Maleski 64), Bardhi, Doriev (Nikolov 85); Rastoder. Booked: None. Manager: Goce Sedloski.

Referee: Michal Ocenas (Slovakia).

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League confirmed updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

Sources indicate that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The fresh dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December.

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals.

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool presently have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.
