📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:44 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 19:02 EST, 13 November 2026.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admitted his side were far from perfect in their Nations League win over North Macedonia – but he believes they ARE moving in the right direction under his stewardship.

The victory puts the Scots one point behind second-placed Slovenia in Group B1, ahead of Monday’s trip to runaway leaders Switzerland.

John McGinn notched a second-half double to secure a hard-earned second win of this campaign and Pocognoli’s first in front of the Hampden crowd.

It has been revealed that ‘We knew before the game that it [a win] will help to build a winning culture,’ he mentioned. ‘And would make the work through the week end with a good feeling.

‘In terms of what we produced on the pitch, I know exactly what we worked on this week. I’m quite satisfied about what I see in some moments of the game, about the work on the ball and off the ball.

‘It was not always perfect but we created a lot of chances that we should score and maybe have a better feeling of the game.

Sebastien Pocognoli got his Hampden win as Scots boss after a 2-1 win over North Macedonia.

Stalwarts John McGinn (left) and Andy Robertson applaud the Hampden crowd at full-time.

‘Off the ball, I think we were quite aggressive. We recover a number of balls that we managed well in some moments of transition.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We created a big chance for Billy [Gilmour] from this also. So that’s a new approach of the game.

In a recent development, ‘We created chances and we had a lot of pressure in the side of Macedonia. After the first goal I think we need to learn not to drop the intensity. Because after the first goal for five minutes I really feel like we dropped the intensity and the focus. So, it’s something that we need to fix.’.

Asked whether his side need to be more clinical, Pocognoli added: ‘Yes, probably. But I prefer to talk about this with creating a lot of chances. We should score two or three. And probably we should have kept a clean sheet. So that’s really the critical aspect and the demanding aspect.

‘But it’s part of the challenge and we are early in the challenge to try to fix this for the future.’.

Talisman McGinn put the Scots ahead on 54 minutes before Elmin Rastoder headed the visitors level against the run of play shortly after, with McGinn then stepping up to convert what turned out to be the winning penalty after a foul on Ben Gannon-Doak with 16 to play.

The Aston Villa midfielder has now taken his tally to 24 for the international team – just six behind legends Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

His manager is confident that it is only a matter of time before the 32-year-old is standing alone as his nation’s top scorer, and believes McGinn will have plenty of opportunities to smash the record playing in his team.

John McGinn scored from the penalty spot to clinch an unconvincing victory.

In a recent development, he stated: ‘I’m more focused on the collective challenge and goals. And I believe if we can build something nice around the collective, then John will one day break the record.

‘We created a lot of chances through these five [Nations League] games together. The individual record is key, but I always focus on the collective package.’.

McGinn admitted that chasing the record is in the back of his mind and stressed his relief that he’s back among the goals after a lean spell at international level.

‘It’s been something that’s been in the back of my head, but obviously the results haven’t been the way we’ve wanted,’ mentioned McGinn.

‘The team come first, but whether it’s myself, Scottie (McTominay), Che (Adams), anyone that’s going on the scoresheet at the minute, we’ll take it.

‘It’s been a bit of a dry patch for me over the past year or two on the goal front, so I’m delighted to get back on that trail and hopefully the same again Monday.

In a recent development, ‘I feel good. I’ve still got many years to go, but the first priority is getting Scotland back to another major tournament and we’ll take it from there.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio è intervenuto Raffaele De Leonardis (sindaco di Qualiano): “Quali sono i progetti da affiancare al centro sportivo del Napoli?
  • Quanto mi hanno dato fastidio le fake news attorno a questo?
  • Industry observers note that I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio è intervenuto Raffaele De Leonardis (sindaco di Qualiano): “Quali sono i progetti da affiancare al centro sportivo del Napoli? Dopo la firma ho già pensato a cosa fare attorno alla zona. Quella sarà una cittadella dello sport, perché affianco ai terreni dove sorgerà il centro sportivo c’è uno stadio, ci sono campi da tennis e abbiamo in animo un palazzetto dello sport e una piscina. Oggi c’è la parte più difficile, quella della burocrazia e infrastrutture. In poco tempo che mi rimane come sindaco mi metterò a disposizione. Quante volte è saltata la trattativa con il Napoli e perché? La prima volta è saltata per il prezzo d’acquisto. Il Presidente De Laurentiis doveva valutare l’investimento. I primi terreni con destinazione urbanistica si parlava di 100 euro a metro quadro. Non c’era bisogno della Zes. Servivano 20 milioni di euro. Non era nelle disponibilità e intenzioni della società. Perché poi bisognava costruire il centro. E comparando con il Viola Park, finanziato dal 20% del Coni, ci fu un primo stop. Successivamente, la Zes paventava di superare vincoli urbanistici, allora si è cominciato a parlare di terreni agricoli. E quindi si è riallacciato il rapporto perché c’erano terreni che rientravano nei desideri della SSC Napoli. C’è stata una visita, sotto la pioggia, il famoso 30 marzo dell’anno dello Scudetto. Il Presidente del Napoli mi invitò allo stadio Maradona, vidi Massimo Boldi, c’era Serena Brancale, c’era De Martino. Quanti vaffa mi sono preso dal Presidente? Abbastanza (sorride ndr). Nell’ultima riunione c’era Chiavelli, c’erano Testa, Discepolo, c’era anche Edo e lì ho capito che forse c’eravamo. Se De Laurentiis si è messo in auto per vedere le distanze dalle stazioni ai terreni? Sì, la prima volta che venne a visitare i terreni prima di Napoli-Milan fece questo percorso in auto. Il Presidente De Laurentiis chiedeva quanto distasse dalla stazione di Afragola, ed erano circa 20 minuti, dalla stazione di Ponte Riccio al centro sono 10 minuti a piedi e da Varcaturo o zone residenziali dei giocatori sono 8 minuti di auto e dallo stadio sono 20 minuti con la tangenziale. Dall’aeroporto ancora meno, 12-13 minuti. De Laurentiis percepiva che la posizione era buona. Fece però un passo indietro in merito alla storia dei rifiuti tossici, si era spaventato, ma non era vero.

Quanto mi hanno dato fastidio le fake news attorno a questo? No, sono il Sindaco di Qualiano, ne sento tante. Però penso che ci sono solo pensieri in negativo. Ma pensiamo anche in positivo. Tutte queste problematiche potrebbero nascere, magari con la Zes. Ma noi che ci guadagniamo? Niente! C’è uno strumento di legge, sono stati fatti i migliori investimenti, noi stiamo sperando che non venga approvato? De Laurentiis ha firmato un atto notarile, un preliminare condizionato e se arriva l’autorizzazione, si trasforma automaticamente in definitivo. Lui che se ne fa di un terreno agricolo!? La Zes ha sette linee guida. Una delle linee riguarda l’attività produttiva per quanto riguarda turismo e sport. Noi non ci opporremo, perché sarebbe da folli. Chiederemo le infrastrutture che dovranno essere realizzate e aiuteremo il Napoli a realizzarle. Noi stiamo rispettando la legge. Se il prof Discepolo presenta il progetto definitivo in 10-15 giorni e partono i 90 giorni della Zes, seguiremo il countdown. Sentivo parlare di un’autorizzazione preliminare per il muro di cinta, con autorizzazione dei proprietari. Se ci sarà un laghetto? Non so se è un vezzo, ma servirà per irrigare i campi. Sarà a mo’ di cisterna. Se ci saranno hotel? Ci saranno sicuramente le stanze per i giocatori. De Laurentiis tiene tanto alla cantera, penso che farà anche un convitto per i giovani”.

Spurs finally score... but still lose

📅 16 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, they scored.
  • Recent findings suggest that it could have been something different.
  • It has been revealed that “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, they scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

Recent findings suggest that it could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, highlighted this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

It has been revealed that “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

According to recent reports, yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

Recent findings suggest that rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Recent findings suggest that big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

It has been revealed that “I see him training every day,” Iraola noted. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he demonstrates is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

Is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a newly introduced contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

In a recent development, his touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Sources indicate that ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some key saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

In a recent development, spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo remarked.

Recent findings suggest that he was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

"A Steven Gerrard type of strike" 😍Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady analyse Dominik Szoboszlai's wondergoal 🪄 pic.twitter.com/h9QTuP8lZc.

"They've done themselves proud!" 👏Conor Coady on Lewis Koumas performance for Liverpool 🔥 pic.twitter.com/3JGkuY7Eye.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

In a recent development, “I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

Industry observers note that “But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no concerns. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is newly introduced, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi noted. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

According to recent reports, “We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

It has been revealed that tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Liverpool ‘showing concrete interest’ in Bundesliga wonderkid Jurgen Klopp likes

  • The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.
  • The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

It has been revealed that christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a latest contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

“I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract currently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

According to recent reports, liverpool, it has to be noted, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

In a recent development, falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The significant issue facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

Il Borussia Dortmund ha diramato un comunicato ufficiale in merito a Samuele Inacio, attaccante classe 2008 seguito anche da Inter e Juventus. Il talento convocato anche da Mancini in Nazionale si è infortunato al menisco durante la partita dell'Italia Under 21 contro il Belgio.

Ecco il comunicato del Borussia Dortmund: "Samuele Inacio ha subito una lesione al menisco durante la partita della nazionale Under 21 italiana contro il Belgio all'inizio di questa settimana, che ha richiesto un intervento chirurgico. L'attaccante diciottenne non sarà a disposizione del Borussia Dortmund per diversi mesi.

Il direttore sportivo del BVB, Ole Book, ha dichiarato: "Questo infortunio è estremamente spiacevole. Soprattutto per Samu, ma anche per il Borussia Dortmund. Samu riceverà tutto il nostro supporto nei prossimi mesi per tornare in piena forma".

Inacio, ovviamente, salterà Borussia Dortmund-Inter, match valido per la sesta giornata di League Phase di Champions in programma il 9 dicembre prossimo.

  • Nato a Monza il 16 agosto 2008, da padre italiano e madre azera, Mezzotero possiede la doppia nazionalità italiana e azera ed è uno dei giovani talenti sui quali il club blucerchiato ha deciso di puntare per il proprio futuro.
  • In a recent development, il suo percorso calcistico è iniziato tra Azerbaigian e Canada, prima di proseguire nel settore giovanile dell’Atalanta.

Recent findings suggest that L’U.C. Sampdoria comunica di aver rinnovato il contratto relativo ai diritti alle prestazioni sportive del calciatore Lorenzo Mezzotero. L’attaccante si è legato al club blucerchiato fino al 30 giugno 2030 (con opzione a favore dello stesso club per ulteriore rinnovo fino al 30 giugno 2031).

Nato a Monza il 16 agosto 2008, da padre italiano e madre azera, Mezzotero possiede la doppia nazionalità italiana e azera ed è uno dei giovani talenti sui quali il club blucerchiato ha deciso di puntare per il proprio futuro.

In a recent development, il suo percorso calcistico è iniziato tra Azerbaigian e Canada, prima di proseguire nel settore giovanile dell’Atalanta. Nell’estate del 2024 è approdato alla Sampdoria, dopo l’esperienza in Spagna con il Fundación Marcet, entrando a far parte dell’Academy blucerchiata e continuando il proprio percorso di crescita.

Recent findings suggest that il lavoro svolto nel settore giovanile gli ha permesso di bruciare le tappe e conquistare progressivamente spazio in prima squadra. Finora sono quattro le presenze collezionate con la maglia blucerchiata, impreziosite dalla prima rete tra i professionisti, realizzata nell’ultima gara casalinga vinta con la Virtus Entella. Un traguardo significativo che testimonia il percorso di crescita del giovane attaccante e la fiducia riposta in lui dal club.

Industry News: Named: Premier League team of the season so far as Erling Haaland, THREE Chelsea players and a surprise addition from Sunderland make the cut

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 04:56 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • The international break has rolled back around and with it a chance to take stock of the Premier League season so far.
  • The first ten games of the new campaign have thrown up a few surprises – none of three  promoted teams find themselves in the drop zone at this stage and the race for Europe is wide open with teams such as Brighton and Everton excelling.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 02:00 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 04:56 EST, 14 November 2026.

The international break has rolled back around and with it a chance to take stock of the Premier League season so far.

The first ten games of the new campaign have thrown up a few surprises – none of three  promoted teams find themselves in the drop zone at this stage and the race for Europe is wide open with teams such as Brighton and Everton excelling.

Here is a look at the players who have defined the opening weeks as Daily Mail Sport, in collaboration with stats gurus Sofascore, compile our team of the season so far...

Many will be surprised to see the Argentine's name here instead of Arsenal's David Raya or Brighton's Bart Verbruggen, but despite Chelsea's defensive woes it is their £7million summer signing that makes the cut.

Martinez has been out for the last three games after sustaining a nasty head injury away at Everton but his average match rating remains the highest out of all the division's shot-stoppers.

A look at the stats tells you why. Despite only keeping one clean sheet so far, Chelsea's new No1 has prevented 1.64 goals, had 13 high claims and 0 errors leading to goals.

The substantial man has also looked extremely competent with the ball at his feet, something that Blues keepers have struggled with in previous years, and has even created three chances from his own box so far this season.

Emiliano Martinez has been out for three weeks with a head injury he sustained at Everton but has still done enough to make our team.

There was always going to have to be at least one of this Brighton team in our XI. We all knew they were an excellent outfit coming into the season but perhaps even Fabian Hurzeler  may not have envisaged his side sitting second after ten games.

Recent findings suggest that the linchpin of this side has of course been their skipper, Lewis Dunk. A local boy who came through the ranks at Brighton and has spent virtually his entire career at the club, he continues to impress at 34 years of age.

In a recent development, dunk has played in nine of Brighton's ten games this season looking solid in each, leading his side to six wins and keeping a clean sheet in each victory. And his personal defensive stats make for excellent reading as well – he has won 22 aerial duels and registered 31 recoveries already this season.

But there are some things that can't be quantified, such as Dunk's impact on the  Brighton dressing room and the guidance he gives such a young squad which must be immense – after all, he is a year older than his own manager.

Next up is another old school English centre-half who has captained his team to an excellent start to the season.

The big man is rolling back the years as the Toffees look to push for Europe.

In recent years the Toffees have become far more familiar with the bottom of the table than the top but at present are making a serious push for the European places and are at the moment in sixth place, level on points with fifth.

And the 33-year-old has been vital to David Moyes's newly introduced system, providing stability and strength to a defence that has conceded just ten goals – with only Arsenal (five), Brighton (seven) and Leeds (eight) conceding fewer.

Again similar to Dunk, Tarkowski's stats show the veteran's ability to adapt to the demands of the modern game, having 108 line-breaking passes, creating four chances and one significant chance so far this season.

The skipper has also come up trumps in close games, bagging a crucial goal in a 1-1 draw at Bournemouth and getting an assist in the 1-0 win over Ipswich.

Completing the back three is the only one out under 30, but is also the man with the highest average match rating in this team.

Considering Tottenham's defensive record this season, one of their defenders making it in may come as a bit of a shock but anyone that has watched the north Londoners this season will know that 26-year-old Van Hecke is hardly the reason for their woes.

The Dutchman has been magnificent since moving from Brighton and reuniting with his old boss Roberto De Zerbi, playing every single minute of the Premier League season so far.

Van Hecke epitomises the modern centre-half, having the second most one-line breaking passes (162), the most two-line breaking passes (37) and the most passes into the final third (138) out of any player in the league – and has even bagged two goals for Spurs as they have started to pick up some form.

Despite Sunderland's poor start, the Black Cats' skipper anchors our midfield with the highest average match rating in his position this campaign. Most would have been expecting Pascal Gross to take this position in an XI such as this considering his eight goals and assists and all-round stellar showing this season.

Xhaka is a surprise entry considering Sunderland's form but the stats tell us that the skipper is still performing.

But the boffins have Xhaka here instead and the numbers show why. The Swiss international has excelled in a number of areas despite Sunderland's faltering start having the second-most passes into the final third (132) and the joint most line-breaking passes into the box (21).

Moving onto the midfield, we have perhaps the most electrifying winger in the league  this season.

Manchester City have tailed off with three defeats on the spin but Jeremy Doku still remains a major source of headaches for the league's full-backs and a full-time entertainer for us viewers.

When he first joined the league the Belgian was criticised for a lack of consistency but recently he appears to have put that all behind him. Doku does only have one goal and one assist this season, but that does not tell the full story.

He has completed the most dribbles in the league this season (27), won nearly 60 per cent of his duels and has created 4.25xG while on the pitch.

He also provided us with arguably the performance of the season so far when he changed the game off the bench away at Liverpool, scoring a goal-of-the-season contender to down the Reds.

The first and only man from the champions and league leaders to get into our team is Bukayo Saka.

Saka appears to be getting back to his best as the champions get off to an excellent start in their title defence.

It was always going to be hard for the man the fans call 'Starboy' to keep up his form from last season but in actual fact his desire to bring more silverware to the Emirates appears more prevalent than ever.

We all know what he can do going forward and the Englishman has netted three goals in the league, but this year he has improved his defensive game massively, winning 43 duels, 11 tackles and registering 23 recoveries already.

Saka has struggled with his fitness for the past year or so and although he has played their first seven Premier League games, has been on the sidelines since mid-October with a thigh injury.

Despite a testing start to the season, Chelsea are the team with the most players to make the list – though few will quibble with this man's inclusion.

Morgan Rogers proved himself to be a special talent at Aston Villa and there won't be many Chelsea fans doubting the wisdom of paying £117million for his services after his flying start.

Morgan Rogers has been a revelation at the bridge thus far, scoring six goals in all competitions and assisting five more.

The Englishman has lit up Stamford Bridge with six goals and five assists in all competitions and has instantly formed a deadly front three with best friend Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro.

The Blues have struggled for form under upcoming manager Xabi Alonso but no criticism can be laid at the feet of Rogers who will hope his goals can bring some much-needed consistency to west London.

Sources indicate that completing the midfield is a man who is finally getting his flowers after months of quality and consistency. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is one of the many reasons Everton fans are excited for the first time in a while.

The Englishman became an instant fan favourite at the Hill Dickinson after moving from Chelsea last year but this season has gone up a gear in every way, running  games from start to finish with surgical passing, clever dribbling and an incredible work rate.

In a recent development, only seven players have covered more ground in the league than his 101km (63 miles), and he has also contributed three goals and an assist – as well as delivering a magnificent 79 defensive contributions. His spot in this team could not be more deserved.

Going into the strike-force these next two names are simply must haves, and the first of the two is the mercurial Joao Pedro.

Joao Pedro has the best goals and assists ratio to games in the league with eight in six games.

Recent findings suggest that after an excellent debut season in blue the Brazilian took the risk of taking on the infamously cursed Chelsea No9 shirt. But it appears to have only spurred him on further as he has enjoyed a  stellar start to the campaign in front of goal.

It only took him two minutes to get on the score sheet this season in Chelsea's opening game away to Fulham and he just hasn't stopped scoring since.

Pedro has five goals and three assists in just six Premier League games and has become a menace for opposition defences. Unfortunately for gaffer Xabi Alonso his side have been unable to match that consistency, having won five, drawn one and lost four in the league.

But the Spaniard will hope to have his star man back soon – in the six games Pedro has managed to play this season the Blues have lost just one.

It would not be an elite Premier League XI without this man in it.

According to recent reports, even with all the controversy surrounding Manchester City, Erling Haaland manages to roar on and continue scoring at an alarming rate. It is yet another season where he props up the Premier League goal scoring table with nine in ten games.

For a  City side in transition away from a decade under Pep Guardiola Haaland's goals this season have been so crucial in smoothing the process and getting important wins.

According to recent reports, the big Norwegian has bagged winners against rivals Manchester United, Ipswich and Coventry as well as netting the vital opener in their 3-0 win at Anfield. Yet again,  he is proving he is the ultimate goal machine.

SSC Napoli Training Center – Gli azzurri si sono allenati in vista della prossima gara di campionato, sabato alle 20:45 contro il Torino al Maradona. Il gruppo è stato impegnato in una seduta pomeridiana svolgendo attivazione e lavoro tecnico-tattico.

Tutti i calciatori sono rientrati dagli impegni con le nazionali.

Alex Meret, in seguito a un trauma subìto in allenamento, si è sottoposto a esami strumentali, presso il Pineta Grande Hospital, che hanno evidenziato una frattura della quinta vertebra lombare.

Il calciatore azzurro ha già iniziato l’iter riabilitativo.

It has been revealed that torna d'attualità in casa Inter il futuro di Alessandro Bastoni. Il contratto del centrale nerazzurro è in scadenza nel 2028 e il Barcellona, dopo essere stato molto forte su di lui un anno fa, potrebbe tornare a bussare presto. Lo riporta Matteo Moretto sul canale YouTube di Fabrizio Romano.

In a recent development, "Io ho parlato un anno fa di Barcellona prendendomi anche gli insulti. Voglio dire che un anno fa dissi che il Barcellona si era mosso concretamente su Bastoni incontrando gli agenti e informandosi sui costi: ho anche aggiunto che era davvero vicino a prenderlo. Dal punto di vista contrattuale e del sì del calciatore le parti non erano così distanti, anzi. Poi dopo alcune riunioni interne il Barça ha deciso di investire i soldi in un altro modo ma soprattutto Flick, per una questione di caratteristiche tecniche e per lo stile di gioco che vuole, Bastoni non ha convinto fino in fondo.

Ecco perché il Barcellona ha deciso di non investire quella somma elevata per prenderlo. Però vi dico che è vero che le trattative con il rinnovo con l'Inter vanno a rilento e confermo un'altra volta che Deco stravede per lui: e sta cercando e cercherà di capire insieme a Flick se ci possono essere i margini per andare avanti in questa operazione che un anno fa era imbastita".

Industry News: RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: I'm told control over transfers was key to Mauricio Pochettino taking Man United job. It seems they finally have a manager bullish enough to hold Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox to account

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 09:10 EST, 14 November 2026.

It has been revealed that it only happened once. But if you search for it, there is footage. The date was February 23, 2000 and the place was the old Wembley Stadium. England 0-0 Argentina, the kind of friendly best forgotten, except for a single line of trivia.

It has been revealed that of all the games played by Jason Wilcox and Mauricio Pochettino, this was the sole example of them sharing a pitch. Wilcox was given the full 90 at a point when Kevin Keegan was low on options for the left wing and Pochettino came on with 35 minutes on the clock and kicked a few people.

Recent findings suggest that he was good at kicking people, Pochettino. He flattened Paul Scholes once, then he nudged over David Beckham and twice he got stuck into Emile Heskey. But Wilcox was in a safe zone on the other side of the field that night. While Pochettino indulged his hobby, Wilcox kept out of harm’s way.

In a recent development, we might ask at this juncture if either of them ever changed their spots. But it’s more interesting to ponder what comes next, now they have been pitched together again at Manchester United.

United needed a massive bull to replace Michael Carrick and they have got one. Wilcox’s preference? Well, United’s director of hopeless football quite fancied Eddie Howe, according to the whispers, and Howe is far from a shrinking violet, but he’s not Pochettino. And Pochettino certainly isn’t Carrick.

In a recent development, pochettino won’t drive to work for three days straight while knowing his race is run. And he won’t have the same patience for incompetence from those below or above.

Manchester United needed a substantial bull to replace Michael Carrick and they have got one in Mauricio Pochettino.

Pochettino is not the sort of manager to drive to work for three days straight while knowing his race is run, like Carrick did this week.

According to recent reports, with any luck, United knew this when they reached an agreement that was a decade in the making. If they did, it would demonstrate some self-awareness at last, because United have badly needed the right blend of bruiser and diplomat in that seat.

They have cried out for someone who isn’t too nice, too loyal, too whiny or too undermined by their own shortcomings to have the kind of rucks that are needed for change. By that logic, United may have invited their own worst enemy to dinner, or their best chance of a solution.

It has been revealed that there have been few managerial appointments in recent years as inherently fascinating as this one. That instinct is partly driven by the thought it has all arrived a touch late – when United favoured Ole Gunnar Solskjaer to replace Jose Mourinho, it was a sliding-door moment for all parties.

Industry observers note that but there’s another way of viewing this and that comes from the opposite angle. Maybe this is the perfect time, based on the qualifications needed to operate within the modern version of United.

There is no doubt that Pochettino has lost some of his sheen since his masterful handling of Daniel Levy at Tottenham, but what did he gain? He managed the vastest collection of footballing egos at PSG, worked under a convoluted tier of meddlers in the madhouse of Chelsea and was confronted by presidential interference in his time with the US national team at the World Cup.

Two schools of thought can exist here. One is that he failed to tear up any trees in each of those assignments. But the other talks to the point we are making: United require a manager who can navigate their unique brand of chaos and the new guy knows the dance.

Pochettino won’t ever thank Donald Trump for the Folarin Balogun fiasco in the summer, but Sir Jim Ratcliffe would have to work awfully hard to cause him a more uncomfortable press conference.

Industry observers note that the scale of Pochettino’s challenge is obvious. In the micro, that means applying a playing style built on hard running to a squad that jogged its way to embarrassing statistics under Carrick. In the macro, it will be his challenge with Wilcox and a recruitment team that effectively cost Carrick his job.

Pochettino has had plenty to deal with as USA coach, not least the meddling of Donald Trump.

Pochettino has the authority to challenge (above, from left) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox over United's failing transfer policy.

Talking to one of Pochettino’s former colleagues on Friday, the expectation is that greater control over transfers will have been a key tenet of those negotiations with United.

As predictable as that might sound, it was a huge bone of contention for him at Chelsea and United’s failures in this area are clear. Time will tell if any promises are honoured.

Sources indicate that but Pochettino has got what he wanted and pursued. His desire for the post has never been disguised, which can be mapped as a trail of breadcrumbs from that bottle of red he once shared with Sir Alex Ferguson all the way up to carefully planted mentions of the club in gatherings with media.

Recent findings suggest that there were some acts of reassurance necessary for the final step, of course, and doubtless it will sting to leave the US - his farewell tears on Friday showed as much. But not enough to inspire a second thought.

To look back over Pochettino’s other stints in England, one main memory stands out from his time at Tottenham and I’ve cited it in this space previously.

It traces to September 2016, when Pochettino was on the rise and had a game approaching against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City. In attempting to coax a decent line in the press conference, a few of us killed time before his arrival by digging up old footage of Pochettino’s Espanyol beating Barcelona, when he and Guardiola were on opposing sides.

Sources indicate that within the clip was an unexpected gem, because Pochettino murdered the Brazilian Ronaldo in a challenge. He took the ball, sure, but demolished the man, too, and his boot ended up shoulder-high. We were watching this when Pochettino wandered over and requested a replay – when it was shown, he laughed maniacally.

As a player, he always saw the value in a good reducer. And it’s a trait that might well be needed at United. If Wilcox and the other cronies upstairs don’t up their game, they might find that Carrington offers fewer hiding places than the old Wembley.

Pochettino's fondness for the USA job was apparent by his farewell tears on Friday.

Was Tom Brady ever in the Blues' building?

Industry observers note that tom Brady has left Birmingham, but was he ever really there? Across three years, he attended only four games.

The club is on a steep upward trajectory and there is no doubt that the Brady association helped on their commercial side.

It has been revealed that but I recall speaking to one Blues shareholder a couple of seasons back, and after attempting to establish some tangible detail about their star investor’s contribution, there was a period of silence. When I asked how often Brady might dial into meetings, there was laughter.

In this era of celebrity ownership of our football clubs, it’s easy to get blinded by a famous name. And easier still to get drawn in by suggestions of expertise that they have carried over from a different space.

But in the vast majority of cases, they are little more than mascots without the costume.

Tom Brady makes a rare appearance at a Birmingham match in 2025.

Great delivery from Cummins - but it's not over yet.

Pat Cummins stood for 70 minutes on Thursday and answered questions about Sandpapergate.

The Australia captain refused to budge, both from the microphone and his position that Usman Khawaja was incorrect in his claim that the entire team was in on the plot to cheat against South Africa in 2018.

It’s hard to know what was more impressive – Cummins’ commitment to answering every question, or his delusion in believing that it would be the last time he discusses it.
